classification_reasons: Spec is not tight in the article's sense even after round 3: it hits sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth' end to end, and Flagged concern 3 accepts a residual heuristic-parsing gap (unlisted wrappers, decoded/piped content) rather than eliminating it, closed only partially in CI by the sandbox layer and not at all on native Windows.

Blast radius is wide: shell_guard.py's decide() runs on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase, by hand and in CI; plugin/ci/settings.ci.json and plugin/ci/run_phase.py's ci_settings_file gain a new sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite rule read by every CI phase job; three pre-existing tests (test_ci.py, test_evals.py x2) have their contracts changed on purpose.

No existing test exercises a Bash/PowerShell write to a guardrail or locked test file today -- that bypass is exactly the intent's finding -- so the planned behavior is new, not already covered by current tests, even though the plan correctly orders reproducing-tests-first and reproducing tests are to be written before the fix in phase (c).
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's Proposed outcome (every instance of the authz-by-tool-route pattern fixed, each proven by a test, an eval case for the class) against the round-3 spec.md/plan.md. Both named instances (protected_paths.py, test_file_lock.py) are still covered by one new hook with no scope drift; the eval case is still owed, now correctly handed to phase (e) rather than attempted in (c). No drift toward 'something nearby'.

Spec and plan, closely, against the three review rounds: cross-read every 'round 3 review, item N' citation in spec.md and plan.md against evidence/fix-requests.json's actual round-3 review body (id 5465295155) item by item (items 1-13: the three pre-existing-test updates named and reasoned, template/.claude/settings.json dropped with the protected_paths.py precedent cited, framework-evals.yml/case-0006 dropped as a follow-up with the GITHUB_TOKEN reason, case 0002 deferred to (e) with case.py's --force behavior cited, the parser declared self-contained, the sandbox block naming .claude/framework as directories and the _ANCHORED_RULE precedent, the Acceptance line purged of the scanner's own literals, the route.py:468 sentence added, the cd/non-literal tests named in Acceptance too and 2>&1/>/dev/null added to the negative list, plan.md's Files/Order-of-work/Risks/Proof all rewritten to match). Every item is reflected accurately; found no item the final spec.md/plan.md silently dropped or contradicted. All open Flagged concerns in spec.md now start with 'decided'.

Verified a sample of the design's own factual citations directly against the current code rather than trusting the prose: plugin/hooks/hooks.json's actual matcher entries for plan_sync.py (two entries, Bash/PowerShell each gated on 'git *'), production_gate.py (one Bash|PowerShell entry, no 'if'), and panel_blind.py (Read|Grep|Bash|PowerShell|Write|Edit|MultiEdit) match spec.md's 'Today' paragraph exactly; plugin/ci/run_phase.py:1067's _ANCHORED_RULE regex (Read|Edit only) matches the cited reason for a second rule; plugin/hooks/protected_paths.py:48's GLOBAL_PROTECTED and plugin/gate/checks.py:1269's check_test_lock docstring and :1666's eval_dir line match the claims built on them; plugin/scan/route.py:468's change_type ternary matches the 'unbounded -> feature' claim; tests/test_evals.py:522/602 and tests/test_ci.py:605 are the exact lines plan.md says will change; evals/cases/0005-hooks-loaded and plugin/evals/run.py exist as cited. No hallucinated path or line number found in a sampled check.

Proof: phase (b) produces no toolchain logs by design; plan.md's Proof section lists tests still to be written in phase (c) and is explicit that nothing about eval cases runs this session. The runner's own stale records (gate-b.json, run-b.json, claude-b.json, adversarial-review-b.json as committed, panel/b-items.json) all carry an earlier head (985ac9d9... or no head) than this round's feed340c and were not used for or against this verdict -- they belong to an earlier round's gate check, not this diff.

Blast radius: confirmed the diff is scoped to changes/0002-.../{spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/**} only -- no plugin/template/doc source file is touched in phase (b), consistent with the design-only phase. sdlc.yaml confirms 'auth' is a real risk_list item and that it is accepted (risk_accepted: [auth] in status.yaml, matching decision 24's by-hand route with risk_accepted_by left empty, as round 2's review explicitly asked for).

Policies: security-baseline rule 1 (authorization not inferred from tool route) is the stated source of the requirement; coding-standards rule 2 (reuse) is honored by reusing protected_paths/test_file_lock's matching primitives while deliberately not reusing production_gate's parser (reasoned, reproduced); coding-standards rule 4 (no weakening) is addressed by naming the three pre-existing tests whose contracts change on purpose, with each named and justified rather than silently touched. One process gap found and weighed, not escalated on: evidence/fix-response.md (required by plugin/commands/sdlc-fix.md step 6, one line per review request) documents rounds 1 and 2 of PR #144's review but has no entry for round 3 (review id 5465295155), even though round 3's 13 items are all reflected in the current spec.md/plan.md. This is a documentation/traceability gap in the fix round's own record, not a defect in the design the diff ships, and it does not change whether phase (c) can build from spec.md/plan.md as written -- kept as an observation, not a reason to escalate, per REVIEW.md's bar (breaks behavior, leaks data, or breaches a policy).

Tests: no test code exists yet; re-checked that plan.md's Order of work still puts the reproducing tests first (imported inside test functions or in a new test_shell_guard.py so a failure cannot abort collection), still requires the tests to be seen failing against current code before the fix, and that the Acceptance/Proof sections describe tests that would actually exercise the Bash/PowerShell bypass (literal guardrail write, plugin-root form, protected_paths entry, locked-test-file fixture, PowerShell forms, cd/resolution and fail-closed cases, and a negative list) rather than merely re-asserting the plan's wording -- a bug that let any of these through would fail a named test, not just the design's prose.
